parsed.explanation: The combined regime criminalises same-sex conduct (20 years plus mandatory whipping) reaching foreign nationals, while all 13 states criminalise cross-dressing for Muslims with no definition of 'transgender dressing'. State-sanctioned targeting of trans people is documented (2020 'full licence' order; 122 officers hunting one woman). Recent raids are visitor-facing: November 2025's 208 arrests included 31 foreign nationals held despite a magistrate rejecting remand, with detainees publicly leaked, followed by another raid days later. Arrest means birth-sex placement and documented male-ward sexual violence. Offsetting this, private-conduct enforcement is uncommon, tourists are rarely targeted, legal aid and judicial pushback function, and no visa bar on trans visitors exists. Net: high risk, below the routine-arrest anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: No explicit visa rule against trans visitors; Registration Department routinely rejects gender-marker changes and the 2016 pro-trans ID judgment was overturned in 2017, so documents issued abroad are the only reference and mismatch scrutiny is possible.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry denial or deportation policy for trans travellers; the only stated policy (2001, gay diplomats) is unsourced as to current operation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/appearance mismatch during a raid or spot-check can convert an inspection into arrest under 377B or state religious provisions.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented raids: 208 arrested 28 Nov 2025 in the capital including 31 foreign nationals whose embassies intervened, another sauna raided in Penang days later; release delayed despite a magistrate rejecting remand; prison terms with birth-sex male-ward sexual violence documented; 2014 strip-search/sexual assault of a trans woman by religious officials.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Legal-aid organisation mobilised bailors; magistrate rejected remand extension; embassies intervened for foreign detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Venue raid → arrest → birth-sex custody; public leaking of detainees' faces magnifies outing exposure for visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: All 13 states and the capital district maintain Sharia enactments barring Muslim men from 'dressing as women', enforced by religious departments with no legal definition; one state extended court-ordered 'rehabilitation' to one year in 2022; Terengganu/Kelantan/Pahang counselling detention provisions.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Federal court struck down one state's cross-dressing provision (2024) and 16 of another's provisions, but on federalism grounds only — federal Penal Code liability untouched.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Non-Muslim visitors escape the Sharia layer but remain exposed to Penal Code 377A/B and 377D at any raid or police encounter.

care_services.exposure: Documented discriminatory denial of health care to trans people; 1982 fatwa bars Muslims from sex-reassignment surgery; conversion therapy practised and promoted by politicians and religious leaders; national blood centre bars homosexual/bisexual donors.
care_services.interaction: An injured or ill outed visitor entering hospital care faces documented hostility; emergency-care refusal risk is real but not separately sourced for visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: July 2020 Religious Affairs Minister gave the capital's religious department 'full licence' against transgender persons; 122 officers mobilised to hunt one trans woman (2021); government-funded 'rehabilitation' retreats (1,733 attendees); LGBT media censorship; Nov 2024 Kelantan entertainment amendments banning LGBTQ-promoting activities.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2022 communications hate-speech code covers sexual orientation; international bodies condemned the 2020 order.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises both the probability of identification and the severity of any encounter, including for foreign visitors present at targeted venues.

minors_guardians.exposure: Conversion therapy openly promoted by politicians and religious leaders; no youth-specific health-care or medication findings in the record.
minors_guardians.protection: Adoption law is orientation-neutral, but this is resident-facing and not traveller protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor gains no documented mitigation; a minor's exposure follows the same raid, custody and care pathways as an adult's, unaddressed specifically.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Three trans women killed in under two months (record through 2019) alongside documented police mistreatment and impunity; venue detainees publicly outed via leaked names and faces in 2025.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented killing after 2019; no trans-specific violence rate given against which to judge frequency.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Impunity for anti-trans violence combines with official targeting to weaken any reliance on police protection after an assault.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime law; identity-card ruling overturned 2017; High Court denied challenge to the cross-dressing law; Islamist opposition blocks reform; release delays despite favourable rulings show remedies are slow.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Magistrate rejected remand extension; legal-aid group mobilised bailors; Home Affairs Minister floated revisiting 377 provisions days after the raid.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial, episodic judicial and civil-society pushback mitigates but does not reverse state-directed enforcement, so recourse reduces rather than removes exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra excludes and humiliates but never imprisons or charges. Here a visitor faces a 20-year-plus-whipping statute, documented arrests of foreign nationals in raids, birth-sex custody with sexual-violence history, and an explicit state order authorising action against trans people. Severity is materially higher than exclusion-only.

Similar but somewhat lower: Ostravia pairs birth-sex prison placement and a cross-dressing statute with slow remedies, brief sentences and formal execution prohibition. This dossier adds a recent, repeated raid pattern including foreigners, a state anti-trans enforcement order, and documented killings with impunity — a heavier state hand than Ostravia's.

Higher than 0.15-B: Saruth detains transgender visitors routinely after secondary inspection, holds them in abusive cells for months, and courts accept police summaries without evidence. Here enforcement against private conduct is uncommon, tourists are rarely targeted, a magistrate rejected remand, legal aid and embassies secured releases, and no capital penalty is attached to gender presentation.

Lower than 0.55-B: Tambera-style exposure is administrative — secondary screening, refusal of admission, slow appeals. This dossier documents criminal liability, mass arrests with foreign nationals held, official anti-trans enforcement authorisation, and impunity for killings, which are categorically more severe than administrative border friction.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is a layered one: a federal Penal Code with severe penalties that reaches tourists, plus Sharia cross-dressing provisions in every state, plus documented official authorisation to act against transgender people. The visitor escapes the Sharia layer only if non-Muslim, and never escapes 377 exposure at a raided venue — the November 2025 and December 2025 raids prove this reaches foreign nationals in practice, with detainees publicly outed. Outing itself is engineered by raid practice and media leaks. State-sanctioned targeting (tier 2) and custody exposure (tier 1 for a trans woman placed by birth sex) dominate. Offsetting weight is genuine but partial: private conduct is rarely enforced, tourists are rarely singled out, a magistrate, legal aid and embassies produced releases, and a minister floated reform. Those show functioning pockets of recourse, not a protective regime; combined they lift the score above the routine-arrest anchors but leave it in High Risk.
